topics.label: Course Introduction and Lecture Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces herself, the cancer lecture series, and the core learning outcomes regarding environmental carcinogens, testing methodologies, and tumor initiation and promotion.

topics.label: Understanding Cancer Etiology: Genetics, Environment, and Epidemiology
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics introduce cancer as a genetic and evolutionary disease driven by an interplay of endogenous cellular processes, genetic predispositions, and environmental exposures, as evidenced by global epidemiological patterns.

topics.label: Biological and Chemical Carcinogens and Mechanisms of DNA Damage
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail specific infectious agents, dietary toxins, radiation, and chemical carcinogens, focusing on how they are metabolically activated to cause direct DNA damage and mutations.

topics.label: Tumor Promotion, Chronic Inflammation, and Host Susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore non-mutagenic mechanisms of carcinogenesis, distinguishing tumor initiators from promoters while examining the roles of chronic inflammation, tissue microenvironments, and developmental stages of life.

topics.label: Methodologies for Identifying and Proving Carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate the experimental, genomic, epidemiological, and in vitro methods used to detect carcinogen exposure, determine mutational signatures, and assess carcinogenic risk.
